description: THE MB-4 CROSS-LUMP TOPO-NAMING GOLDEN (docs/design/multi-body.md §MB-4): a downstream fillet names ONE edge of the SECOND lump of a multi-lump body and resolves it to EXACTLY ONE edge -- proving stage-1 edge signatures resolve per-lump on a Compound body. Six features: (1)-(4) build two disjoint 20x20x20 cubes A (x[0,20]) and B (x[30,50]) exactly as boolean-union-two-disjoint-cubes; (5) a `boolean` union with allow_disjoint=true -> ONE two-lump body (a Compound, lumps ordered by centroid x: lump 0 = A at x=10, lump 1 = B at x=40); (6) a `fillet` radius 2 mm naming the vertical corner edge of LUMP 1 (body B) at x=50, y=0, z in [0,20] by its stage-1 EdgeSignature (a straight line (50,0,0)->(50,0,20)). That edge exists ONLY on lump B -- lump A has no edge at x=50 -- so the absolute-world-coordinate signature resolves to exactly one edge (no cross-lump ambiguity), and the fillet rounds it while leaving lump A untouched. The body stays two lumps (shells=2): lump A is an unmodified 6-face cube, lump B is a 7-face filleted cube. Locks the MB-4a modifying-op path on a multi-lump body: fillet_body relaxes its single-solid guard to lump-count-preserving == k (k=2 here), OCCT fillets only the owning lump, and the result reassembles as a lump-sorted Compound. Byte-identical GLB across an interpreter restart + STEP multi-solid round-trip.
derivation: Expectations are HAND-DERIVED analytic values, cross-checked against the harness (geometry-gates skill). Two 20^3 cubes = 16000 mm^3 (lump A x[0,20], lump B x[30,50], both y,z in [0,20]). The fillet r=2 rounds ONE vertical edge of lump B (the x=50,y=0 corner, height 20). The removed sliver is a prism (height 20) of the corner cross-section = the corner square [48,50]x[0,2] (area 4) MINUS the quarter-disk (radius 2, centre (48,2), area pi) that the rounded corner keeps solid -> removed cross-section area = 4 - pi, removed volume = 20*(4 - pi).

surface_area = 4712 + 22*pi = 4781.115038378975 mm^2. Derivation: start from the two-cube 4800; filleting lump B's vertical edge (a) removes a 2x20 strip from each of B's two adjacent side faces (x=50 and y=0): -2*(2*20) = -80; (b) rounds the corner of B's top and bottom cap faces, each losing the (4 - pi) corner cross-section: -2*(4 - pi) = -8 + 2*pi; (c) adds the quarter-cylinder fillet face (radius 2, height 20): arc length (pi/2)*2 = pi, area pi*20 = 20*pi. Net 4800 - 80 - 8 + 2*pi + 20*pi = 4712 + 22*pi. Measured 4781.1150383789745 (deviation ~5e-13).

centroid = (24.973625822389..., 10.010261751083..., 10) mm. z = 10 exactly (both cubes and the sliver are symmetric in z about 10). x,y shift because the removed sliver sits at lump B's x=50,y=0 corner: the sliver's cross-section centroid (square [48,50]x[0,2] centroid (49,1) area 4 minus quarter-disk centroid (48 + 8/(3pi), 2 - 8/(3pi)) area pi) is (~49.554, ~0.447); as a z-prism its 3D centroid is (49.554, 0.447, 10) with volume 20*(4-pi)=17.168. final = (8000*(10,10,10)+8000*(40,10,10) - 17.168*(49.554,0.447,10)) / 15982.832 = (24.9736, 10.0103, 10.0). Measured (24.97362582238927, 10.010261751083917, 9.999999999999998) -- matches the hand derivation to ~1e-11.

bounding_box = [0,0,0]..[50,20,20]: the fillet only rounds an INTERIOR corner of lump B, it does not move any outer bound (the x=50 and y=0 planes still bound B away from the filleted corner). Exact, measured deviation <= 5e-16 (a GProp ulp on the y-min).

topology = 13 faces, 27 edges, 2 SHELLS: lump A untouched (6 faces, 12 edges, 1 shell); lump B filleted on one vertical edge -> 6 box faces + 1 fillet face = 7 faces, 12 + 3 = 15 edges (the sharp vertical edge is replaced by the fillet face's two tangent-line edges + the arc splits at top/bottom -- same 7/15 as the single-body MB-3 boolean-union-then-fillet golden), 1 shell. Totals: 13 faces, 27 edges, 2 shells. shells=2 confirms the fillet is lump-count-preserving (it did not merge or sever the lumps).

mesh (linear 0.1 mm / angular 0.1 rad): lump A is 6 planar quads -> 24 vertices / 12 triangles; lump B's planar faces + the tessellated quarter-cylinder fillet face bring the total to 178 vertices / 152 triangles. Recorded from the deterministic tessellation (a curved fillet face's facet count is a pure function of the deflection, asserted exactly and byte-identical across an interpreter restart).

GLB byte size is deliberately NOT pinned here: it is asserted deterministic (byte-identical) by the runner within one kernel version, but pinning the absolute size would break on every glTF-writer upgrade without geometric meaning.
tolerance_rationale: Measured first, then set (geometry-gates skill: never copy a bound blindly). This is a two-lump Compound body: an untouched planar cube plus a cube with one OCCT-filleted vertical edge (BRepFilletAPI on the owning lump only). Analytic anchors are exact closed forms -- volume 15920 + 20*pi, surface_area 4712 + 22*pi, and the inclusion/exclusion centroid -- all independently hand-derived above. Measured deviations vs those analytic values (2026-07-18, build123d 0.11.1 / OCCT 7.9, planegcs 0.8.0): volume ~2e-12 mm^3, surface_area ~5e-13 mm^2, centroid x/y ~1e-11 mm (the fillet centroid carries a touch more GProp integration noise than a pure box) and z <= 2e-15, bounding_box <= 5e-16. Documented ceiling 1e-9 is ~90x the observed worst case (~1e-11, centroid) -- headroom for platform FP variation across OCCT builds and the STEP round-trip re-measure, while staying 5 orders of magnitude tighter than the standing kernel linear tolerance (1e-7 m -> 1e-4 mm). The solver contributes zero error (both squares shape-pinned -> solved == input). Loosening this further requires a reviewed kernel-level justification recorded here and in docs/GEOMETRY-QA.md.
